# Assignment: Enterprise AI Product & Automation Fellow Challenge

## Objective

This assignment is designed to test whether you can do the actual work of an Enterprise AI Product & Automation Fellow at Ajaia.

We want to assess your ability to:
- design a reusable AI-enabled workflow for a real business process
- think clearly about inputs, outputs, automation logic, and human review
- scope a practical version one of a product or internal tool
- document your system clearly enough that another operator could use or build it
- show product judgment, systems thinking, and builder instinct
- use AI tools in a practical, high-leverage way

This role is about internal leverage, reusable systems, rapid prototyping, and clean documentation. Your submission should reflect product thinking, clarity, and AI-native execution.

## Time Limit

Please spend **no more than 3 hours total** on this assignment.

We are not looking for a full production build. We are looking for the quality of your system design, product judgment, and execution thinking.

## Scenario

Assume Ajaia wants to create an AI-powered CRM management workflow to help track conversations, opportunities, and next steps across multiple clients and prospects.

Today, important information is often spread across email threads, notes, and individual follow-ups. Ajaia wants a system that helps the team stay on top of relationship management and sales progress without relying on manual tracking alone.

Your job is to design a reusable AI-enabled workflow or lightweight product concept that helps:
- track client and prospect activity across email-based interactions
- organize accounts by stage or contracting progress
- surface reminders or notifications when it is time to re-engage
- reduce missed follow-ups and fragmented relationship context

You do not need to build a production-ready application. We are looking for a strong version-one concept with practical workflow logic.

## Tasks

### 1. Define the Problem and User

Define the core problem your workflow or product is solving.

Explain:
- who the primary user is
- what is broken or inefficient in the current process
- why this workflow is worth solving

### 2. Define the Inputs and Outputs

Describe what information goes into the system and what should come out of it.

### 3. Design the Workflow

Design the end-to-end workflow for how the system would operate.

Include:
- how data enters the system
- how AI is used within the workflow
- what should be automated
- what should require human review or approval
- how users interact with the system over time

You may present this as a process flow, product concept, screen flow, or systems diagram.

### 4. Scope Version One

Define what version one of this workflow or product should include.

Include:
- the minimum useful feature set
- what you would leave out initially
- the main risks or failure modes
- how you would evaluate whether v1 is working

### 5. Create a Documentation Asset

Create one documentation asset that would help another operator, PM, or builder understand the system.

Examples:
- a one-page product spec
- a workflow diagram
- an operator playbook
- a system logic overview
- a simple PRD

### 6. Build a Lightweight Prototype or Mockup

Create an artifact that helps us understand how the system would actually work.

This could be:
- a low-fidelity interface mockup
- a sample dashboard or table structure
- a prototype flow
- a structured wireframe

We are not evaluating visual polish as the main criteria. We are evaluating clarity of product thinking and workflow design.

## AI-Native Workflow Note

AI usage is a core expectation of this role.

Please include a short note describing:
- which AI tools you used
- where they helped
- how they accelerated your process
- what product and systems decisions were yours

We are not evaluating whether you avoided AI. We are evaluating how effectively you used it.

## Walkthrough Video

Record a short walkthrough video explaining:
- the problem you chose to solve
- how your workflow operates
- what the inputs and outputs are
- what is automated versus human-reviewed
- what you included in version one and what you left out
- how you used AI in your workflow

Please upload this as an **unlisted YouTube video** and include the link in your submission.

## Deliverables

Please submit the following:

- `1 concise deck, doc, or PDF explaining the problem, user, workflow, inputs, outputs, and v1 scope`
- `1 documentation asset such as a PRD, workflow diagram, or operator playbook`
- `1 lightweight prototype, wireframe, mockup, system diagram, or sample dashboard artifact`
- `1 short AI workflow note`
- `1 walkthrough video link`

## Submission Format

Please submit **one Google Drive folder link** containing all materials.

Your folder should include:
- your main concept document or deck
- your documentation asset
- your prototype or mockup artifact
- your AI workflow note

In the application text field, paste:
- your **Google Drive folder link** which must be publically accessible so we can view (sharing permissions anyone with link can view)
- your **unlisted YouTube walkthrough link**

## What We Will Evaluate

We will evaluate your submission based on:

- quality of systems thinking
- clarity of inputs, outputs, and workflow logic
- product intuition in scoping version one
- practicality of the human-versus-automation split
- quality of documentation and communication
- usefulness of the prototype or mockup artifact
- AI-native workflow maturity
- clarity of communication in your walkthrough

## Constraints

- Maximum time: **3 hours**
- Keep the workflow realistic and operationally useful
- Prioritize clarity, leverage, and practicality over complexity

## Optional Stretch

If time permits, you may include a short note on:
- how this system could evolve into a more robust CRM intelligence layer
- what metrics you would track after rollout
